correctness.rationale: The compactly supported measure has a product of masks whose tail is nonvanishing and analytic locally: the translated compact complex neighborhoods have a summable bound on deviations from one. For the mask geometry, a nonzero sum of two unit vectors determines their unordered pair, since their product is the sum divided by its conjugate; a vanishing total of four unit vectors therefore pairs them antipodally. This yields the three known line families. At one scale two pivots occur only for the phases (−1,−1,+1); that fixes all coordinates to integers and yields exactly the equal-low-valuation condition. Across k<l, the higher pivot is +1 at k, forcing both others to be −1 there. The higher factor can thus vanish exactly when the nonzero high coordinate and the difference of the low coordinates have equal finite valuation; neither low coordinate can pivot again, and the high coordinate can pivot at only one scale. The three distinct directions are the permutations of (0,1,1), with absolute determinant 2. A pivot derivative of each vanishing factor is nonzero, so Taylor orders add exactly as one or two, even when the real zero lines of a single factor cross. For a specified high coordinate, the probability of a junction with low valuation a is 2^(−3a−3). For a triple the high valuation is a+j with j≥1, and the odd-part difference has valuation j with probability 2^(−j), giving weight 2^(−3a−2j−3). These sums, times three choices of high coordinate, give 3/7 and 1/7. Fixed moduli equidistribute in the centered cubes; discarded large-a or large-j cases require a coordinate in a high power-of-two divisibility class, bounding their upper density by a vanishing geometric tail. Zero high coordinate and coincident low coordinates do not create triples. A separate exact bounded modular recount (bounded_junction_check.py) reproduced (junctions, triples)=(1500,528) at R=7 and (108252,37200) at R=31. It corroborates the lattice arithmetic, not the unrestricted real geometry or the limiting densities. The supplied verify_tetra.py was inspected, not executed.

Also credit exact mathematical overlap of the indexed even-scale cancellation theorem at b=2: it covers both lattice densities and the at-most-two-level bound on the lattice, and its congruences recover the lattice two-scale test. value.rationale: The equal-weight dyadic tetrahedral measure is a standard affine self-similar object, and its known Fourier zero locus does not distinguish ordinary zeros from intersections or Taylor multiplicity. A complete real local classification explains why a two-line crossing can still be first order, identifies exactly where a second factor creates a transverse triple, and makes those singularities countable on the lattice. The geometry/order correspondence is the value beyond the already indexed lattice density calculation; a replay of those density numbers alone would not suffice.
